$comment: SYNTHETIC. This is not an anatomical name index and must never be shipped as one.
The real index comes from the asset pipeline (plan task 4) as coverings.json, with
cells derived from BodyParts3D meshes and an ICBM152 parcellation. Until it lands,
this file lets the research model, both browse modes and the solid-colour layers be
built and tested end to end. The CELLS ARE INVENTED, chosen only to exercise the
shapes that matter:
- a containment chain  (inferior frontal gyrus BV-L-04 contains areas 44, 45, 55b)
- a midline structure spanning both BV hemisphere roots
- overlapping structures in one cell (7th rib and lower lobe of left lung)
- structures in both frames, so a cross-atlas selection can be exercised
`authoredAgainst.status` in a dataset says `fixture` while its mappings are authored
against this file. Switching to the real index is a dataset edit, not a code edit.
## Two id namespaces, and why
`HCP-MMP1:<area>` is that parcellation's own label namespace, so those ids are real.
`ATLAS-LABEL:<kebab-name>` is a PLACEHOLDER namespace for everything else. The gross
anatomical structures here have UBERON and FMA accessions, and the curator did not
have verified accession numbers to hand — so rather than write plausible-looking
numbers that would be unfalsifiable without checking the ontology, the id is the
label itself. Crosswalking ATLAS-LABEL onto the accessions the real coverings.json
uses is a named part of stage B, owned jointly with the asset pipeline. An invented
accession would resolve to the WRONG structure and look authoritative doing it.
